sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *advertir que* with the indicative or the subjunctive from B1 Unit 38, and *recordar* from A2. The rule you learned in the first lesson of this unit is the whole point here: a warning or a reminder can pass on a fact, or it can tell someone what to do. A fact takes the indicative. Something to do or not to do takes the subjunctive, as in the reported orders of B1 Unit 38.

sections.title: Warning and reminding
rows: advertir que + indicative (a fact, a danger)
Nos advirtió que el puente estaba cerrado.
advertir que + subjunctive (do or don't do)
Me recordó que la tienda cerraba a las ocho.
Me recordó que cerrara la puerta.
Alertaron de que venía una tormenta.

sections.title: Reminding someone, or remembering
sections.content: *Me recordó* means "he reminded me": the person reminded is the indirect object (*me*, *te*, *le*). Do not confuse it with *recordé* "I remembered". Ask yourself one question to choose the mood: is it information or a task? Information (the bridge is closed, the shop closes at eight): indicative. A task (don't cross, close the door): subjunctive.

items.spanish: Nos advirtió que el puente estaba cerrado.
items.english: He warned us that the bridge was closed.
He warned us not to cross.

items.spanish: Me recordó que la tienda cerraba a las ocho.
items.english: She reminded me that the shop closed at eight.

items.spanish: Me recordó que cerrara la puerta.
items.english: She reminded me to close the door.

sections.content: In the sense of "remind", *recordar* takes *que* directly: *Me recordó que…*, not *Me recordó de que…*. *Advertir* takes *que*, and *alertar* takes *de que*.
